en.headline: Police hold woman, 22, over fake official deposit scam
en.dek: Officers say she showed a fake police warrant card and is linked to eight cases, after one victim transferred nearly 650,000 dollars.
body: Police have arrested a 22-year-old mainland Chinese woman on suspicion of obtaining property by deception, after callers posing as Hong Kong immigration officers and mainland public-security officers demanded a deposit of nearly 650,000 dollars. West Kowloon senior inspector Wai Chun-to of the technology and wealth investigation unit outlined the case on Thursday morning.

Officers said the report was made on 19 September. The callers claimed the victim had taken part in money laundering and asked for the sum as a deposit. The victim transferred the money to a private account named by the callers.

Police said the arrested woman is suspected of helping the callers by delivering forged confidential documents and showing a forged Hong Kong police warrant card. She was arrested on Tuesday near her home. Officers seized a forged warrant card and a forged confidentiality agreement that they said was meant for another victim, and said that stopped a further loss.
The woman is suspected of involvement in seven other cases of the same type and is being detained for investigation. Police have not named her.

zh.headline: 假扮入境處及公安收保證金 22歲女被捕
zh.dek: 西九龍重案組表示，女子涉嫌出示偽造警察委任證，涉及8宗案件，其中一宗事主轉帳近65萬元。
body: 警方拘捕一名22歲內地女子，涉嫌以欺騙手段取得財產。騙徒假扮香港入境處及內地公安人員致電事主，訛稱事主涉及洗黑錢，要求繳交近65萬元保證金。西九龍科技及財富調查組高級督察衞進濤周四早交代案情。
警方說，案件於9月19日接報。事主擔心自己在不知情下涉案，按指示把款項轉入騙徒指定的私人戶口。
警方指，被捕女子涉嫌協助騙徒，向事主送交偽造保密文件，並出示偽造香港警察委任證。人員周二在其住所附近拘捕她，檢獲一張偽造委任證，以及一張準備交給另一名事主的偽造保密協議，阻止了另一宗損失。
女子另涉7宗同類案件，正被扣留調查。警方未有公布其姓名。
